tour.overview:
In 1889, for the centenary of the Revolution, Gustave Eiffel's company built an iron tower 300 metres tall on the Champ de Mars. Many Parisians hated it; it was meant to stand for twenty years. Today it is the symbol of the city. From the tower, the great avenues laid out in the 19th century lead to the Arc de Triomphe, and to the north the hill of Montmartre, once a village of windmills, vineyards and painters, rises under the white domes of Sacré-Cœur.

This private day is about the views and the neighbourhoods of Paris. With a licensed guide and a car, you go up the Eiffel Tower in the morning, see the Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Élysées, and spend the afternoon on the hill of Montmartre, where Renoir, Van Gogh and Picasso lived and worked. You end with a cruise on the Seine, the best way to see how the city's monuments line up along the river.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Paris
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 5 km, with steps and slopes in Montmartre

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Eiffel Tower (second floor; the summit can be added).
• The Trocadéro.
• The Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Élysées.
• Montmartre: Place du Tertre, the Bateau-Lavoir, the vineyard and the Moulin de la Galette.
• Sacré-Cœur.
• The Seine by boat.

WHY THIS WORKS
The car links places that are far apart on foot, and we book the Eiffel Tower and the cruise at times that avoid the longest waits.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors, couples and families who want the great postcard sights of Paris in one day.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer art and history, choose our Louvre, Notre-Dame and Sainte-Chapelle tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Eiffel Tower's summit can close in high wind. Montmartre has many steps; the funicular saves the steepest climb. Pickpockets operate around Sacré-Cœur and the Trocadéro.

days.name: Eiffel Tower, Trocadéro, Arc de Triomphe and Champs-Élysées, Montmartre, Sacré-Cœur and a Seine cruise
days.description:
What to expect: the great views of Paris in one day, with a licensed guide, private car, timed tickets, a cruise and lunch.

Your driver and guide collect you at your hotel at about 8:45 and drive to the Trocadéro for the classic view across the Seine to the Eiffel Tower. You cross the river and go up the tower with your timed tickets. On the way your guide tells the story of the 1889 World's Fair, the 18,000 iron parts and 2.5 million rivets, and how the tower was saved from demolition by its use as a radio antenna. From the second floor, 115 metres up, all of Paris lies around you: the Seine, the golden dome of the Invalides, Montparnasse and Montmartre on the horizon. If you have added the summit, you continue by lift to 276 metres.

The car takes you up the avenues to the Arc de Triomphe, ordered by Napoleon in 1806 after Austerlitz, where the Unknown Soldier of the First World War lies under an eternal flame, and down the Champs-Élysées. After lunch, you drive to the foot of Montmartre. You ride the funicular or climb the steps to Sacré-Cœur, built after 1875 in white travertine that whitens in the rain, and look out over the roofs of the whole city. Your guide then leads you through the village behind it: Place du Tertre, full of painters at their easels, the Bateau-Lavoir where Picasso painted Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, the last vineyard of Paris and the Moulin de la Galette that Renoir painted.

To finish, the car takes you down to the river for a one-hour cruise on the Seine, gliding past the Louvre, Notre-Dame, the Musée d'Orsay and back towards the Eiffel Tower. Your driver takes you back to your hotel at about 17:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:45 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Trocadéro viewpoint.
09:30 – Eiffel Tower (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
11:15 – Arc de Triomphe and the Champs-Élysées.
12:30 – Lunch.
14:00 – Montmartre: Sacré-Cœur, Place du Tertre and the village.
15:45 – Seine cruise (about 1 hour).
17:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Eiffel Tower summit and the Arc de Triomphe rooftop can be added with separate tickets.
• In the evening, the Eiffel Tower sparkles for five minutes every hour after dark; an evening cruise can replace the afternoon one.
• On national holidays the Champs-Élysées may be closed to traffic.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Eiffel Tower tickets to the second floor, Seine cruise, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Eiffel Tower summit, Arc de Triomphe rooftop, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Do we go to the top of the Eiffel Tower?
faq.answer: The tickets include the second floor, the best level for views of the city. The summit can be added if tickets are available; it closes in high wind.

faq.question: Do we skip the lines at the Eiffel Tower?
faq.answer: We book timed tickets, so you avoid the ticket queue. There is still a security check and a short wait for the lifts at busy times.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Eiffel Tower to the second floor and the Seine cruise. Sacré-Cœur is free to enter.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km. Montmartre has steps and steep lanes; we use the funicular and the car to save the hardest parts.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch at a local restaurant. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Can we do the cruise in the evening?
faq.answer: Yes. We can end the day with an evening cruise to see the Eiffel Tower sparkle, with a later drop-off.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the tower, the boat and the painters of Montmartre. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The Eiffel Tower lifts, the cruise and the car make most of the day easy. Montmartre is steep, but the car can reach the top of the hill.

faq.question: Will we be taken to souvenir shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and a light jacket: it is windy on the tower and on the boat. For Sacré-Cœur, respectful clothing.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Clear days in spring and autumn give the best views; summer evenings are long and light until about 22:00.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour, because Eiffel Tower tickets are non-refundable after that. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
